headline: Injured penguins in Chile wear copper vests

sources.title: Copper vests help Chile's penguins heal (AP News)
Innovación en Coquimbo: Pingüinos usan trajes de cobre para acelerar su recuperación y rehabilitación (Cooperativa Ciencia)
La innovadora terapia que ayuda a sanar a los pingüinos heridos (Diario El Día)
Rehabilitan pingüinos con trajes forrados de cobre: así funciona la tecnología chilena que protege sus heridas (El Tiempo)
Copper suits help injured penguins in Chile recover (video, Paraluman News)

chunks.text: Researchers in Chile are {{trying out}} [[snug]] red vests on injured Humboldt penguins. The fabric is [[woven]] with copper and zinc, which may help [[wounds]] {{heal up}} faster. Veterinarians use similar suits on dogs and cats, and a Chilean team {{came up with}} a penguin version. "We began to wonder, why can't this be used on penguins?" the director of a zoo near Santiago told The Associated Press on September 2, 2026.

verbs.correct: To test something to see how it works
verbs.wrong: To wear clothes to check their fit
verbs.why: Shoppers try out a new phone in the store before buying it, and a coach tries out a new player in a practice game. Researchers in Chile are trying out snug red vests on injured Humboldt penguins.
A scraped knee heals up in about a week, and a broken bone can take months to heal up. The team hopes the copper and zinc in the fabric will help the penguins' wounds heal up faster.

verbs.correct: To think of an idea or plan
verbs.why: A student comes up with a topic for an essay, and a company comes up with a name for its new product. A Chilean team came up with a penguin version of the healing suits used on dogs and cats.

chunks.text: A [[nonprofit]] [[rescue center]] in northern Chile {{takes in}} [[stranded]] penguins from the coast. Some are cut by [[fishing nets]] or boat [[propellers]], and others are weak from hunger, said the veterinarian who leads the program. Penguins twist their necks to [[peck]] at wounds and {{pull out}} their [[stitches]], and [[bandages]] had to be changed daily. Staff {{take the vest off}} for treatment and replace it quickly, which {{cuts down on}} handling.

verbs.correct: To accept someone and give them care
verbs.wrong: To gain control of a place or group
verbs.why: A family can take in a stray cat, and a shelter takes in people during a storm. Wildlife clinics on Chile's coast take in stranded penguins, some cut by fishing nets or boat propellers.

verbs.wrong: To recover from a serious illness
verbs.why: A dentist pulls out a bad tooth, and a gardener pulls out weeds after the rain. Penguins twist their necks to peck at wounds and pull out their stitches.

verbs.correct: To remove something that is worn
verbs.wrong: To care for a sick or injured animal
verbs.why: People take off their shoes at the door, and a nurse takes off an old bandage before cleaning a cut. Staff take the vest off for treatment and replace it quickly.

verbs.correct: To reduce the amount of something
verbs.why: A doctor may tell you to cut down on salt, and a family can cut down on driving to save gas. Removing and replacing the vest quickly cuts down on handling of the penguins.

chunks.text: Copper and zinc {{hold back}} bacteria and fungi, and zinc helps new [[blood vessels]] form, so damaged [[tissue]] recovers faster. Chile is the world's top copper producer. The Chilean maker sells a pet version in more than 40 countries. Suits made for four-legged pets tend to {{slip down}} on a bird that stands [[upright]], so designers measured [[flippers]], necks, and tails and tested [[prototypes]] at the zoo before {{sending them off}} to the rescue center.

verbs.wrong: To keep something warm and dry
verbs.why: A dam holds back the river, and a fence holds back the crowd at a concert. Copper and zinc in the fabric hold back bacteria and fungi in the wound.

verbs.correct: To slide to a lower position
verbs.wrong: To make a small careless mistake
verbs.why: Loose socks slip down inside your shoes, and a heavy backpack slips down off one shoulder. Suits made for four-legged pets tend to slip down on a bird that stands upright.

verbs.correct: To mail or deliver something to a place
verbs.wrong: To return something to its maker
verbs.why: A student sends off a college application, and a shop sends off its orders every morning. Designers tested prototypes at the zoo before sending them off to the rescue center.

chunks.text: Chile's Humboldt penguins, a [[vulnerable species]], are declining sharply. Surveys of the main [[breeding colonies]] in 2024 and 2025 found 63 percent fewer [[active nests]] than three years earlier. El Niño warms the sea and {{drives away}} the fish they eat, so parents {{leave chicks behind}} to hunt. The veterinarian said the birds {{put up with}} the vests well and wounds looked better within a day, but the team has not yet proved the vests {{speed up}} healing.

verbs.why: Loud music drives away the neighbors, and a bad smell drives away customers. El Niño warms the sea and drives away the fish that penguins eat.

verbs.correct: To go somewhere without taking someone
verbs.wrong: To not include something in a group
verbs.why: A mother leaves her son behind with a neighbor when she works a night shift, and a coach leaves two players behind when the team flies to a game. Hungry penguin parents leave chicks behind while they search for food.

verbs.wrong: To dress an animal in clothing
verbs.why: A neighbor puts up with noise from the street, and a commuter puts up with a crowded train. The veterinarian said the penguins put up with the vests well.

verbs.wrong: To use all of something completely
verbs.why: A shortcut speeds up a trip to work, and a new machine speeds up the work of a factory. The team has not yet proved that the vests speed up healing.

mainIdea.s: Chilean researchers are testing red vests woven with copper and zinc on injured Humboldt penguins. The vests stop the birds from removing their stitches and may help wounds close faster.
mainIdea.why: The vests were adapted from pet suits, and the copper and zinc in the fabric hold back bacteria while the garment keeps penguins from pulling out their stitches.

mainIdea.s: Rescue centers in Chile have proved that copper vests heal penguin wounds twice as fast as bandages. The suits, first made for dogs and cats, are now sold to zoos in 40 countries.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the team has not yet proved that the vests speed up healing, and it is the pet version of the suit that is sold in more than 40 countries.

mainIdea.s: Scientists in Chile counted the country's Humboldt penguins and found 63 percent fewer birds than in 2021. They blame fishing nets and plastic and want new protected areas along the coast.
mainIdea.why: The 63 percent figure is a drop in active nests at breeding colonies, and the news is about vests being tested on injured penguins, not a plan for protected areas.

lines.text: Did you see the story about the penguins in Chile wearing little red vests?
Red vests? [[I'd pay to see that]]. What are they for?
They're for injured Humboldt penguins. The fabric is woven with copper and zinc, and the vets hope it helps wounds {{heal up}} faster.
So it's like a bandage you wear. Whose idea was it?
Vets have used suits like that on dogs and cats for years. A team in Chile {{came up with}} a penguin version and is {{trying it out}} now.
Why do penguins need one? Can't they just wear a normal bandage?
Not for long. They twist their necks and {{pull out}} their own stitches. The vest stops that, and staff can {{take it off}} for treatment and replace it in seconds.
[[Poor things]]. And the copper actually does something?
Copper and zinc {{hold back}} bacteria, and zinc helps new blood vessels grow. Chile is the world's biggest copper producer, so [[that figures]].
Was it hard to make a suit for a bird?
The pet suits {{slip down}} on a penguin because it stands upright. They measured flippers, necks, and tails, tested prototypes at a zoo, and then {{sent them off}} to the rescue center.
The vet said the birds {{put up with}} it well and wounds looked better within a day. But they haven't proved yet that it {{speeds up}} healing.
[[Too soon to say]], then. Still, those penguins need all the help they can get, right?
Right. Surveys found 63 percent fewer active nests than three years earlier, and El Niño {{drives away}} the fish, so parents {{leave chicks behind}} to hunt.
[[Every little bit helps]]. I hope other rescue centers get the vests too.
